skill.name: browser-use
skill.description: Browser automation skill for Playwright MCP. It helps navigate pages, fill forms, click elements, capture screenshots, inspect page state, and extract web data.
skill.summary: Automate browser workflows with Playwright MCP from Claude, Codex, or Claude Code.
skill.author: AbdullahMalik17

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are false positives from Markdown backticks, JSON schema identifiers, localhost examples, and JSON-RPC bookkeeping. Confirmed risks include shell-based stdio command execution, predictable /tmp PID files used for process control, HTTP MCP transport exposure, unpinned runtime package execution, and arbitrary browser code execution. No prompt injection or covert data exfiltration language was found.

remediation.issue: User-supplied stdio commands run through subprocess.Popen with shell=True.
remediation.suggestion: Accept an argument array, avoid shell=True, or restrict stdio commands to an allowlist of trusted MCP servers.

remediation.issue: The helper script executes npx @playwright/mcp@latest at runtime.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the Playwright MCP package version and document the expected package checksum or release.

remediation.issue: Start and stop scripts use predictable /tmp PID files for process control.
remediation.suggestion: Store PID files in a user-owned runtime directory, validate PID contents, and verify the process command before signaling it.

remediation.issue: The MCP client can send tool requests to any configured HTTP endpoint.
remediation.suggestion: Default to localhost, warn before remote URLs, and avoid sending secrets or authenticated session data to untrusted MCP servers.

remediation.issue: Browser code execution can interact with sensitive authenticated pages.
remediation.suggestion: Require trusted code snippets, keep browser tasks scoped, and warn users before using shared browser context with real accounts.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Runtime Package Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill starts Playwright MCP with npx @playwright/mcp@latest, which downloads and executes the latest package version at runtime. This creates supply-chain and reproducibility risk for marketplace users.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command explicitly uses npx with an @latest package specifier. That is a clear unpinned runtime execution path, although the package is a legitimate Playwright MCP package.

semantic_findings.title: Arbitrary Browser Code Execution Capability
semantic_findings.description: The skill documents browser_evaluate and browser_run_code workflows that execute user-provided JavaScript or Playwright code in the active browser page. This is a powerful intended feature, but it can affect authenticated sessions and expose page data if misused.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation directly describes executing JavaScript and Playwright snippets against the page. The risk is contextual rather than covert because it is part of the advertised browser automation feature set.

content.user_title: Automate Browser Workflows with Playwright MCP
content.value_statement: Manual browser tasks slow down testing, research, and data capture. This skill connects Claude, Codex, or Claude Code to Playwright MCP for repeatable browser actions.
actual_capabilities: Starts and stops a local Playwright MCP server with helper scripts.
Navigates web pages and browser history through MCP tool calls.
Captures accessibility snapshots and screenshots for page inspection.
Clicks elements, types text, fills forms, selects options, and waits for page states.
Runs JavaScript evaluation and multi-step Playwright snippets inside the active browser page.
Calls MCP tools through HTTP transport and an optional stdio transport.
limitations: Requires Node.js, Playwright MCP, Python 3, and local shell access.
Browser actions can affect authenticated sessions and sensitive web accounts.
Does not bypass CAPTCHA, paywalls, access controls, or website terms.
The bundled helper scripts use local processes, network calls, and temporary PID files.

use_cases.title: Test Web Forms
use_cases.description: Automate form completion, button clicks, waits, and screenshots during manual regression checks.

use_cases.title: Collect Page Evidence
use_cases.description: Navigate public pages, capture page state, and extract visible information for structured notes.

use_cases.title: Debug Browser Flows
use_cases.description: Inspect page snapshots, console output, and network behavior while reproducing user interface issues.

prompt_templates.title: Open and Inspect a Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Start the browser MCP server, open the target URL, capture a snapshot, and summarize the visible page sections.

prompt_templates.title: Capture a Visual State
prompt_templates.prompt: Navigate to the page, wait until the main content is visible, and take a full-page screenshot with a clear filename.

prompt_templates.title: Complete a Test Form
prompt_templates.prompt: Use a page snapshot to find form fields, fill the provided test values, submit the form, and report the confirmation state.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Multi-Step Browser Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Execute a trusted multi-step Playwright workflow, capture the final page state, and explain each browser action performed.

output_examples.input: Open a product page and capture its current visual state.
output_examples.output: The browser opens the page, waits for content, saves a screenshot, and reports the page title and visible sections.

output_examples.input: Fill a test signup form with supplied sample data.
output_examples.output: The form fields are completed, the submit button is clicked, and the resulting confirmation message is summarized.

output_examples.input: Extract headings and visible links from a public documentation page.
output_examples.output: The response lists the main headings, visible navigation links, and any extraction limits observed on the page.

best_practices: Use trusted URLs and avoid entering real secrets unless the page is approved.
Capture a snapshot before clicking or typing so element references are current.
Stop the MCP server after browser work is complete to close active sessions.
anti_patterns: Do not run browser code from untrusted prompts or copied web content.
Do not use authenticated accounts on websites that are outside the approved task scope.
Do not point the MCP client at remote servers unless you trust the endpoint.

faq.question: What does this skill automate?
faq.answer: It automates browser actions through Playwright MCP, including navigation, screenshots, form entry, clicks, and page inspection.

faq.question: Does it need a local server?
faq.answer: Yes. The helper scripts start a local Playwright MCP server that receives browser tool calls.

faq.question: Can it browse authenticated websites?
faq.answer: Yes, but only use approved accounts and trusted sites because the shared browser context can preserve session state.

faq.question: Can it extract data from pages?
faq.answer: Yes. It can use snapshots or trusted page evaluation to collect visible page data.

faq.question: Is it suitable for production scraping?
faq.answer: It is better suited for assisted automation, QA checks, and controlled research than large-scale scraping.

faq.question: What should users review before use?
faq.answer: Review the helper scripts, pinned package versions, target URLs, and any browser code before running automated actions.
